newsitem.title: CHINA: Yaskawa, Iwatani in China venture.
newsitem.headline: Yaskawa, Iwatani in China venture.

text.p: Japan's Yaskawa Electric Corp and Iwatani International Corp have decided to set up a joint venture with a Chinese steelmaker to make industrial robots in China, the China Daily Business Weekly said on Sunday.
The venture, Shougang Motoman Robot Co Ltd, is expected to open in September, the newspaper said. Production capacity would reach 800 robots in five years.
Industrial robots manufactured by the venture would be used in automobile, motorcycle, engineering and chemical manufacturing.
Beijing's giant steelmaker Shougang Group would have a 45 percent stake in the $10 million-venture, with Yaskawa holding 43 percent and Iwatani 12 percent, it said.
Yaskawa would transfer technology to the venture, Li Chengtong, assistant president and senior engineer of the venture, said.
Shougang would manufacture at least 55 percent of the robots' parts, with the rest imported from Japan.
Localisation would be carried out gradually, Li said, adding that the venture would eventually export parts it manufactures.
The newspaper gave no further details.
